title: Bowing Kaomoji m(_ _)m: Copy & Paste Bow and Apology Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste bowing kaomoji: m(_ _)m, apology bows like m(。_。)m, thank-you bows m(＿ ＿)m, the Japanese dogeza and orz kneeling, plus polite small bows.
hero_tagline: Text faces bowing low to say sorry, thank you or please, from m(_ _)m to the full kneeling orz. Tap one to copy it.
intro: The classic bowing kaomoji is m(_ _)m. It is drawn from above: the two m are hands flat on the floor, the brackets are the head, and _ _ are eyes closed as the forehead tips down. In Japan a deep bow carries apology, thanks or a request, so the same face can mean any of the three, and the words beside it decide which. The lowest bow is dogeza, kneeling with the forehead to the ground, and orz draws it from the side. If you came looking for ribbon bows to decorate a name, the bow and ribbon symbols page linked below is the one you want.

sections.label: Dogeza & orz
sections.intro: The lowest bow, kneeling with the head to the floor. In orz, o is the head, r the arms and back, and z the folded legs.

sections.label: Small Bows
sections.intro: A nod of a bow for a quick thanks or excuse me, not a full apology.

faq.a: It is a person bowing deeply, seen from above, with both hands on the floor. In Japanese chat it is used to say sorry, thank you, or please, depending on the words around it.

orz is a person kneeling with their head on the floor, seen from the side: o is the head, r is the arms and back, z is the legs. It started as a sign of despair or defeat and is also used for a dramatic apology or for being overwhelmed.
Dogeza (土下座) is a Japanese gesture of kneeling and bowing until the forehead touches the ground. It is the deepest apology or plea. Online it is usually typed as m(_ _)m or orz.
